newsitem.title: USA: Getchell Gold gains after Santa Fe bid.
newsitem.headline: Getchell Gold gains after Santa Fe bid.

text.p: Shares in Getchell Gold Corp rose Tuesday amid a bidding war for Santa Fe Pacific Gold, which owns mine neighboring Getchell's Nevada property.
Getchell owns a 50 square mile (130 square kilometers) property in Nevada west of Santa Fe's Twin Creeks Mine, Getchell chief financial officer Donald Robson said.

Analysts said the upturn in Getchell's stock could be due to investor speculation a suitor might also emerge for Getchell. Getchell was up two at 34-3/4 in late afternoon American Stock Exchange trading.
Earlier Tuesday, Newmont Mining Corp sweetened its offer for Santa Fe, which on Dec 9 agreed to be acquired by Homestake Mining Co.
"With fairly heated merger activity in a nearby property, one would think at some point Getchell itself would be one that someone would be interested in," said Davenport & Co analyst Michael Beall.
Robson declined comment on any bid speculation.
Robson and analysts also noted Getchell's stock, along with those of other gold mining companies, had been under pressure due to recent weakness in the price of gold.
"Getchell came down here pretty hard in the last week or two," DIBC Wood Gundy analyst David Davidson said.

Gold mining shares are now rebounding with the gold market, analysts said. COMEX gold futures for February delivery ended up $1.00 at $359.70 an ounce Tuesday after slipping $10.00 in the previous three sessions.
Echo Bay Mines was up 2/16 at 6-3/16 on Amex. In New York Stock Exchange trade, Barrick Gold Corp gained 3/8 to 26-7/8, ASA Ltd rose 3/4 to 34-1/2, and Placer Dome Inc firmed 1/8 to 20-3/8.
